name: Libya

findings.local_actor: Eastern Libyan authorities (proposed 'Ozon' mobile network); General Authority for Communications and Informatics (GNU, Tripoli) as suspending body
findings.reversal_of: Reported USD 700m Huawei contract to build an eastern Libyan mobile network ('Ozon'), plus all Huawei activity in Libya
findings.summary: Tripoli's telecom regulator suspended all Huawei activity in Libya and voided contracts made outside its licensing framework, after eastern authorities reportedly sought a USD 198m letter of credit toward a USD 700m Huawei deal for an eastern mobile network.
findings.analyst_inference: Reviewer call: reason coded 'regulatory' because the stated grounds are licensing authority and the rival-government split (east vs Tripoli), not a foreign-alignment or security exclusion of PRC equipment; it should not move the map. Tier 3 is the reported contract reversed, but the contract's signature is unverified (only a USD 198m LC request is reported), so tier may be overstated. The USD 700m is a reported, not announced-by-party, figure. Agenzia Nova sidebar mentions a later 'agreement with Huawei for resumption of operations' not read, so still_current left null. Existing Huawei equipment in Libyana/Almadar networks not established.

findings.summary: State-owned LTT and ZTE signed a memorandum of understanding at MWC 2026 covering 4G/5G planning and deployment, fixed wireless access and customer devices, and joint digital services such as e-wallet and CDN; no value or timetable disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: non-binding MOU. Signed after the August 2025 Huawei suspension (LBY-001), suggesting PRC vendor engagement with Tripoli-aligned state telcos continued; this is inference, not stated in the source.

findings.local_actor: Libyan United International for Telecommunication and Technology (LUIC), part of LPTIC
findings.financier: AFR-IX Telecom, Orange and the European Union (system-level funding)
findings.summary: State-owned LUIC (LPTIC group) joined the EU-backed Medusa Mediterranean cable in 2023 to land it at Tripoli and Benghazi; LPTIC launched the Libyan landing project in May 2025, with full landing expected by end-2025. ASN supplies and installs the system.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third: equipment vendor ASN (Nokia, Finland/France); owner-developer AFR-IX is Spanish. The 2022 ASN contract predates Libya joining and does not list Libya, so ASN supplying the Libyan branch is inferred. Tier 4 = landing project launched (construction); ready-for-service in Libya not confirmed in opened sources.

findings.controller: Smart Co for Technology Projects and Artificial Intelligence
findings.local_actor: Smart Co for Technology Projects and Artificial Intelligence
findings.summary: A Libyan private firm launched LibiGPT (beta), billed as the first Libyan national LLM in 7B, 13B and 34B sizes tuned to local dialect, with data stored locally; ministers attended the Tripoli launch but no government role was stated.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2 as a public beta/pilot. Base model undisclosed; the 7B/13B/34B size set is consistent with fine-tuning of a foreign open-weight family, but that is unconfirmed, so base_model null. 'National' scale reflects branding, not state adoption.

research_gaps: Radio/core vendors for Libyana and Almadar Aljadid (including the January 2026 Tripoli 5G launch) are not established; the 2012 Ericsson/Alcatel-Lucent Almadar contract was paywalled and not coded.
Was the August 2025 Huawei suspension lifted? Agenzia Nova references an 'agreement with Huawei for resumption of operations' not read; was the eastern 'Ozon' network built?
Has Medusa reached ready-for-service at Tripoli and Benghazi, and which vendor built the Libyan branch?
Safe-city or surveillance deployments (Huawei, Hikvision, ZTE) in Tripoli or the east, including Haftar-controlled areas; not searched.
Base model and hosting of LibiGPT; any government adoption of foreign model providers under Libya's 2026 national AI strategy.
